around.headline: CCTV captures Bengaluru law student being stabbed after she rejected a marriage proposal
around.summary: Security camera footage showed a woman being attacked after turning down a marriage proposal, per The Times of India. If someone escalates from persistent proposals to threats or stalking, report it to police early (100) rather than waiting for it to turn physical.

around.headline: Car crash exposed the kidnap-murder of a 13-year-old boy by a neighbour over an education loan
around.summary: A string of crashes involving a fleeing car led police to a boy's body in the boot; investigators say the neighbour abducted and killed him in a bid to settle a loan debt, per The Hindu and India Today.

around.headline: Varthur-Gunjur gridlock leaves school buses taking 2+ hours to cover a few kilometres, again
around.summary: Schoolchildren were stranded for hours in East Bengaluru traffic for a second straight day, with nearly 5,000 residents now demanding civic action, per The Times of India and The South First. If your commute runs through Varthur, Gunjur or Whitefield, build in a large buffer or shift travel earlier until this eases.
around.source: The Times of India, The South First

around.headline: Lokayukta traps Central GST Superintendent taking ₹8 lakh bribe in Bengaluru
around.summary: Anti-corruption police caught the officer red-handed accepting the bribe on camera, per NDTV and The Times of India. If any official demands cash to process your file, you can report it to the Karnataka Lokayukta rather than pay up.

around.headline: Karnataka High Court issues sweeping safety guidelines after half of east Bengaluru's PGs found illegal
around.summary: The GBA told the High Court that roughly half the paying-guest accommodations inspected in east Bengaluru operate without licences, prompting new fire and safety norms, per Live Law and The News Minute. Worth checking if your own PG has basic fire exits and a licence displayed.

around.headline: Commodity markets brace for the Trump-Xi summit outcome
around.summary: Analysts are watching the upcoming Trump-Xi talks for signals on trade and energy flows that move global oil prices, per Reuters. Any shift there eventually filters through to petrol and diesel prices at the pump here.

street_smart.title: You're at a government office in Bengaluru to get a routine certificate processed. The clerk says your file has hit a 'technical snag' and is stuck in the queue — but hints that a small cash 'processing fee' handed to him directly, no receipt, will get it moving today. Like the Central GST Superintendent caught today by the Lokayukta taking an ₹8 lakh bribe on camera. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: NDTV, The Times of India and thehindu.com, Sept 18 — Lokayukta police trapped a Central GST Superintendent in Bengaluru accepting an ₹8 lakh bribe on camera. This bribe-solicitation-at-a-government-office mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You need the certificate today, the office is about to close for the day, and the clerk is friendly about it rather than aggressive — making it feel like a normal shortcut rather than a crime.

choices.text: Pay the cash 'fee' quietly since it's a small amount and you need the certificate urgently.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Paying leaves no paper trail, offers you zero protection if the file still doesn't move, and both sides are liable under the Prevention of Corruption Act — you become as exposed as the official if it's ever investigated.

choices.text: Refuse to pay, ask in writing what specific rule or document is causing the delay, and mention you'll raise it with the Karnataka Lokayukta (1800-425-3990) if it isn't resolved through the normal process.
choices.feedback: Correct. Most delays framed as 'technical snags' are just leverage for a bribe — asking for the reason in writing forces a real answer, and naming the Lokayukta escalation path makes most officials back off immediately rather than risk being reported.

choices.text: Walk away and complain to a senior officer in the same office right away, without noting down any names or the clerk's window number.
choices.feedback: Risky. Without the clerk's name, counter number or the date and time, a verbal complaint on the spot is easy to deny — you're better off documenting the encounter before or as you escalate it.

choices.text: Come back another day hoping to get a different, more honest clerk.
choices.feedback: Risky — it wastes a trip, doesn't fix the underlying delay, and does nothing to stop the same demand being made of the next person in the queue.

takeaways: Karnataka Lokayukta's toll-free helpline (1800-425-3990) and its website (lokayukta.karnataka.gov.in) take complaints against any state government official demanding a bribe.
Many Karnataka government services have a guaranteed timeline under the Sakala scheme — if a service is delayed beyond that, the delay itself is a valid, documentable complaint.
Never hand over a cash bribe, even a small one 'to speed things up' — it's a criminal offence for both the giver and taker, with no legal protection if the transaction goes wrong.

quiz.question: Per NDTV and The Times of India, how much cash was the Central GST Superintendent caught taking in a Lokayukta trap in Bengaluru today?
quiz.why: The Lokayukta is Karnataka's anti-corruption body that runs sting operations on state and central officials working within the state.

quiz.question: According to The Hindu and India Today, what led police to discover the kidnap-murder of a 13-year-old boy in Bengaluru today?
quiz.why: Investigators say the boy's body was found in the boot of a car that had been involved in multiple crashes while fleeing, according to police.

quiz.question: Per Al Jazeera, a bomb attack on a mosque today killed at least 16 people in which country?
quiz.why: The blast also injured dozens more, adding to a string of attacks on religious sites in the region this year.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age to be elected as a member of India's Lok Sabha?
quiz.why: The minimum age is lower than for the Rajya Sabha (30 years) or the office of President (35 years).

quiz.question: Unlike Delhi, Kolkata and Varanasi, which major Indian city is notably NOT built on the banks of a river?
quiz.why: Bengaluru instead depends on a network of man-made lakes and a pumped Cauvery pipeline nearly 100 km away for its water supply.
